Util¶

This module offers a bunch of helper functions and utility functions. These functions take into account the difference between symbolic and numeric calculations, and are used in various calculations.

calc_curr_like¶

The probability current from a state \(m\) to a state \(n\) is given by

\[J_{mn} = W_{mn} P_{n} - W_{nm} P_{m}.\]

Due to the nature of the theory, these types of equations show up a lot in calculating the conductances. This function calculates this expression for an arbitrary matrix and vector.

stoch_imp.util.calc_curr_like(m, p)[source]¶

Calculate expressions of current-like form: \(J_{mn} = W_{mn} P_n - W_{nm} P_m\).

Parameters:

  • m (Mat) – The matrix to be used (must be square).

  • p (ConstantMatrix | Matrix | ndarray) – The vector to be used (length must match m).

Returns:

Resulting matrix \(J_{mn}\).

Return type:

ConstantMatrix

deep_simp¶

This function simplifies symbolic objects in place by first simplifying numerically, then symbolically. If the object passed is an instance of (a subclass of) Mat, the internal matrix is simplified.

stoch_imp.util.deep_simp(expr, **flags)[source]¶

Simplify an arbitrary symbolic expression.

Parameters:

expr (Any)

gram_schmidt¶

When orthogonalizing the vectors, a non-canonical inner product is used. This function implements the Gram-Schmidt algorithm using the inner product given by

\[\langle v, w \rangle = \sum_i \frac{v_i w_i}{P^{eq}_i}\]

where \(P^{eq}\) is given as optional input to the function. If no \(P^{eq}\) is given a vector consisting only of ones is used, yielding the standard inner product.

stoch_imp.util.gram_schmidt(v_arr, Peq=None)[source]¶

Orthogonalize a set of vectors using Gram-Schmidt procedure.

Parameters:

  • v_arr (list[Matrix] | ndarray | list[ConstantMatrix]) – List of symbolic vectors or NumPy array (columns = vectors).

  • Peq (ConstantMatrix | Matrix | ndarray | None) – Equilibrium distribution for weighted inner product.

Returns:

Orthogonalized vectors.

Return type:

list[Matrix] | ndarray

inner¶

This is a simple helper function performing the inner product as defined by

\[\langle v, w \rangle = \sum_i \frac{v_i w_i}{P^{eq}_i}\]

where \(P^{eq}\) is given as optional input to the function. If no \(P^{eq}\) is given a vector consisting only of ones is used, yielding the standard inner product.

stoch_imp.util.inner(v1, v2, Peq=None)[source]¶

Compute inner product between two vectors, optionally weighted by Peq.

Parameters:

  • v1 (Matrix | ndarray | ConstantMatrix) – First vector.

  • v2 (Matrix | ndarray | ConstantMatrix) – Second vector.

  • Peq (ConstantMatrix | Matrix | ndarray | None) – Optional equilibrium vector.

Returns:

Scalar inner product.

Return type:

float | Expr
